correctness.rationale: Exactly four zero-based regular-paperfolding prefixes are defined by an odd-part rule. A complete factor-by-factor verification confirms explicit attractors of sizes 5,6,6,7. For each certificate factor its actual full occurrence-span union is computed, position loads are bounded by denominators 1,2,2,8 and integer weight sums 5,11,12,51 yield lower bounds 5,6,6,7 via the elementary weighted hitting-set inequality. Two independent standalone Python checkers with distinct substring-enumeration/bitset algorithms pass on the exact embedded files. No argument from partial enumeration, numerical solver output or asymptotic extrapolation is used; limitations are finite and explicit.

value.rationale: The target lengths are the four consecutive dyadic steps immediately beyond the existing exact regular-paperfolding census through 64, not an arbitrary slice. String attractor size is an established finite-word compression invariant. Closing all four explicit published gaps gives a completed exact dyadic profile through 1024 with meaningful structural plateau/increase behavior and independently reproducible weighted lower-bound certificates. No general theorem or paper-sized result is assumed necessary for this natural exact finite classification.
